  - the audit with exact files and types (rig, pose routes, the ~25 body draw sites, cosmetics flow and DEV gates, death and gore, zombies, the asset rules);
  - measured current cost;
  - a reuse / adapt / replace table;
  - the asset pipeline and runtime format;
  - the skeleton spec and first-person handling;
  - the cosmetic schema, hide masks, compatibility rules and legacy mapping;
  - the chest core and wrist device states;
  - the death path, the performance budget, Phases B–E with acceptance, the Astra contract, risks and open decisions.
- **Key decisions (proposed):**
  - **Skeleton:** bind to the exact 22 `CapturedRig` joints and rest offsets, so every pose route, layer and IK drives the mesh unchanged. Joint indices are authority data (wound parts).
  - **Runtime format:** a deterministic Blender export to a Core-parsed binary mesh library plus a JSON manifest, drawn by a `SkinnedMeshRenderer` (live rig bones, or pooled puppets fed the `bone(b)` matrices `Queue` already gets). Not FBX: an FBX can only be verified by an Editor import, its exports are non-deterministic, and its `.meta`/fileID churn breaks references.
  - **Outfits:** combined per outfit signature, with hide masks dropping covered skin.
  - **Body skin:** a new `body:modular` entry, so old clients fall back to Standard.
  - **Death:** per-vertex ragdoll regions, region masks, authored stump caps, detached weights; bisect by bake, cut and rebind; shader wound decals.
- **Measured (Core, offline):**
  - Standard Full / Reduced / Low: 48 parts, 7,782 / 4,056 / 1,584 tris (16,924 / 8,664 / 3,168 verts).
  - Sheldon Clothes: 4,342 / 2,652 / 1,284 tris. Prototype: 2,616 tris.
  - 48 materials per skin; one instanced draw per part, i.e. 48 draws plus 48 shadow draws per (skin, tier) in view.
  - Zombie kinds: 21 sections, 4,662–7,132 tris at Full.
  - Skinned estimate: 1 draw and 1 shadow draw per pilot, 4–7 k tris, about 9–14 k verts, a new per-frame skinning cost and no instancing (to be measured in Unity in Phase C).
- **Findings for the owner:**
  - The joints give a stocky 1.70 m figure (hips .57 m, shoulders 1.10 m), not the reference's long legs.
  - The existing chip-select "display wrist" is the free hand (usually the left), so a right-wrist device moves it.
  - The account backend allowlists cosmetics fields, so a new persisted field needs a Sites deploy.
- **Astra:** proposed contract in section i of the doc:
  - a `look` normalized map string on prefs, the account `NativeCosmetics`, `NativeSeat` and `NativeSeatFrame`, with MaxLength 512;
  - the backend allowlist and `modular` added to `BODY_SKINS`;
  - DEV gates and `look:<id>` grants;
  - looks resolved by seat id for corpses and killcam;
  - no gameplay read.
- **Checks (actual):** `git diff --check`; secret and model-name scan of the diff; Python unittest discover in `unity/ChipArenaConversion`. The measurements come from a scratch console build of `Core/*.cs` (not committed) and a decode of `SourceModels.json`.
- **Not run:** Unity Editor, Windows, GPU timing, two clients (docs-only change).
- **Animation/timing/networking impact:** none in this change; the plan keeps hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement and networking unchanged.
- **Next:** owner decisions (section j: proportions, height, wrist side, default outfit); Phase B review against the section c spec; then Phase C.

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: muzzle flashes that light the scene (merged into shared)

- **Branch/base:** `claude/muzzle-flash`, from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` at `ac94d72`; shared `d555363` (Astra's #292) merged in at `ece1ba1`, and `b0e0a12` (`claude/expedition-quota-ui`) at `1721ba7`. Implementation `43ccfa8`, `ee118ad` and `5ece43a`. Presentation only: no rules, timing, damage, hitbox, cooldown, movement, network or save change; the flash and light read the shot events and `Actor.LastShot` that already replicate. Merged into shared and the builder; not published.
- **Owner request:** better muzzle flashes, still using lighting.
- **Before:** one three-petal star for every gun, sitting 3-5 cm ahead of the muzzle face. Its light borrowed a projectile Unity point light that was free. Those lights are culled from the view layer, and `NativeBlockLit` (every dressed map) has no add pass. So the flash never lit the floor, walls, kit or first-person gun, and under machine-gun fire the bullets held all three lights.
- **Mechanism:** a dedicated 4-slot muzzle-light block, `Resources/NativeMuzzleLight.cginc` (`_MuzzleLightPos/_MuzzleLightColor[4]`, `_MuzzleLightCount`, early out at 0). `NativeBlockLit` adds it in `BlockLights`. `NativeSourceLit`, `NativeZombieLit` and `NativeLit` add albedo × it as base-pass emission, wrapped .35 on bodies. So it lights every map, the view model and the bodies, in the base pass with no extra draws.
  - Why not the existing slots: the actor slots are on only at three maps, and the 8 practical slots are already filled by map picks and the kit.
  - Why not Unity lights: each costs a forward-add draw per object and light, and they skip layer 10.
- **Light (`Core/NativeMuzzleLight.cs`):**
  - Envelope: a 3-4 ms attack, then exp decay τ 45/65/40 ms (pistol, rifle, machine gun), gone by 6τ. Peak 2.6/3.0/2.2, range 6/7.5/6.5 m, warm white.
  - Bursts: machine-gun and Overdrive bursts merge into one sustained, seeded 90 Hz flicker per shooter, never stacked; Fan the Hammer works the same way.
  - Clock: the replicated shot times, so host, guest, late joiner and killcam agree.
  - Picker: the nearest 4 shooters (ties by id), first person preferred. In first person the light softens within .5 m and is capped at .65, so the view gun never whites out.
  - Budget: Combat glow, Reduced effects, low tier and Alarm lights set 4/2/1/0 slots and the gain. Calm gives a slow glow with no strobe.
  - Uploader: `Runtime/NativeMuzzleLights.cs` uploads it after the weapon effects. The stage frames (Draft, Intro, Entrance, just after their pinned `WardFieldOff();EnterStage();`), the rooftop and a map look change clear it.
  - The old pulse is removed from `NativeCombatGlow`.
- **Flash (`Core/NativeMuzzleFlash.cs`, drawn by `NativeWeaponFxShapes.Muzzle`):**
  - Layers: core, fireball, plume, a petal star from the muzzle device, vent jets, pods, seeded sparks and smoke wisps. Older rounds' wisps linger.
  - Anchor: the measured crown of each gun and skin.
  - Per weapon:
    - Pistol: the compensator, 3 petals and 2 top-port jets, punchy, 50 ms.
    - Rifle: the brake, 3 petals and 6 side jets (+1 top port at Full detail), larger, 80 ms.
    - Machine gun: the hider's 4-slot X, 45 ms with flicker.
    - Prototype skin: a plain cross with no vents.
  - Chips: ricochet collars, the vacuum bell and boomerang vanes cover the vents they sit over, and multishot pods flash on their own. The module presentation (`MuzzleChips`) hands the flash the seat's kinds and the gun's sockets, so Core and the weapon effects never name the modules (ChipModuleChecks' rule, caught by the first run5b).
  - Kits: Fan the Hammer and Overdrive grow the flash, and Overdrive heat whitens it.
  - Tiers: the Low model tier drops the vents, as the models do; sparks and wisps follow quality; first person has its own lead, glow and tilt so the sights don't hide it.
- **Files:**
  - New: Core `NativeMuzzleFlash.cs`, `NativeMuzzleLight.cs`; Runtime `NativeMuzzleLights.cs`; Resources `NativeMuzzleLight.cginc`; Tests `MuzzleFlashChecks.cs`; their metas.
  - Changed: Core `NativeWeaponFx.cs` (old look removed); Runtime `NativeWeaponFxDraw.cs`, `NativeWeaponFxPresentation.cs`, `NativeChipModulePresentation.cs`, `NativeCombatGlow.cs`, `NativeLighting.cs`; the four shaders; Tests `WeaponFxChecks.cs`, `Program.cs` (`--muzzle-flash`, which also runs ChipModuleChecks).
- **Checks run:**
  - `--muzzle-flash` PASS: 32,811 muzzle-flash checks, 479 weapon-effects checks, 16,281 Gun-kit checks and 36,257 chip-module checks.
    - Crowns sit on the drawn faces, and vents are within 1 mm of their slots.
    - With 8 machine guns there are at most 4/2/1/0 lights, the nearest ones; host = guest = late joiner; 0 bytes over 600 frames × 8 shooters.
    - Central Station's darkest spot, before → peak (/255): pistol floor 6→114, wall 2→104, zombie skin 3→84, first-person hand 0→36; rifle 6→128 and 2→121; machine gun 6→107 and 2→99.
  - `WeaponFxChecks` re-measures on purpose: flash life 60-100 → 40-90 ms; the plume replaces the side flame; core ≤ .25; the old projectile-light pin becomes "no muzzle pulse takes a projectile light".
  - Related groups PASS: `--zombie-light --ward-lighting --station-visuals --killcam --zombie-gore --hazard-kit --weapon-sockets --bow --ironworks-visuals --rounds-visuals --cyber-ranged`. After the chip fix and the `b0e0a12` merge, `--muzzle-flash --zombie-light --station-visuals --killcam --weapon-sockets --hazard-kit` pass again.
  - Unity compile stub: runtime and editor build OK.
  - glslang HLSL front end (stub UnityCG): every `NativeBlockLit` pass and the three surf functions compile, linear and gamma.
  - Offline before/after renders: SwiftShader, with the real shader blocks and draw code.
  - run5b on `5ece43a`: rc1-rc5 all 0. That covers the Unity compile stub, the full managed suite and the relay stage (813 PASS lines, the real WebSocket relay included), 140 Python tests OK (1 skipped), the source package and the diff check.
  - The first three run5b runs failed rc2, on contracts these changes broke, and each was fixed without touching the check:
    - ChipModuleChecks: Core and the weapon effects named the modules.
    - MapLookChecks: the pinned `EnterStage` body.
    - WardLightingChecks: the pinned `WardFieldOff();EnterStage();` pair.
- **Not run:** Unity Editor import and the platform shader compile, Windows play, two-client and killcam on real clients, GPU timing.
- **Cost:** CPU per frame is a ≤512-event scan per gun rig, ≤16 picker offers and 3 global uniform sets, with no allocation. GPU is a uniform branch when no gun fires; otherwise 4 iterations of about 15 ALU per pixel in those base passes.
- **Risks:**
  - The muzzle light casts no shadows on blocks or bodies, so it can reach through thin walls within its 6-7.5 m range.
  - On bodies the light is base-pass emission, so it goes through the surface shaders' finalcolor tone and fog; that wasn't checked in Unity.
  - Killcam rounds can light up to 50 ms late, as their flash already does.
  - Astra: no gameplay part.
- **Next:** owner review in the Windows build (dark Central Station, first person under machine-gun fire).

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: Expedition city grown, a longer walk to the instances (exp-layout-7; merged into shared)

- **Branch/base:** `claude/expedition-city-bigger`, from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` `ac94d72`, fast-forwarded to `d555363` (#292) before the first commit, then merged with `b0e0a12` (the quota and ending UI; no conflict). Implementation `aee9153`. Merged into shared and the builder; not released.
- **Owner request:** "I will also like to make the expedition city still a little bigger (I want players to walk further still.) Afterwards, lets begin improving the design quality of the city". This is the first part; the graphics pass is a separate task.
- **Design** (`docs/EXPEDITION-HUB.md` "The city grown"): everything beyond the city's edge (|x| or -z past 44 m) moves 24 m outward (the wilds, the instance frontages and doors, the corner masses); straddling blocks stretch. Each band is an outer quarter: the forecourt's axis ends against a landmark (the Exchange east, the Union Hall west, the Tram Depot south), so the route turns up a 7 m lane (or a 4 m back alley) round it, comes out on a square before the old checkpoint and sees the instance's beacon again down the wilds. Rows close the bands; cover and five spawns per quarter; each quarter is a mid-ring hub zone.
- **Before → after** (navigation graph, any-angle; run 6.8 m/s): town 192 x 156 → 240 x 180 m (+44%), street 7,978 → 9,386 m², nodes 9,505 → 11,040 (all reached). Sanctuary slots to the join circles 81.0 / 79.0 / 80.2 → 111.8 / 109.2 / 111.3 m (x1.38-1.39; 11.9 → 16.4 s running, 12.2 s sprinting); route gate to circle 67.1 / 65.1 / 66.3 → 97.9 / 95.2 / 97.4 m (x1.46-1.47); the route record gate-to-doorway 72.9 / 71.7 / 72.9 → 107.0 m. 24 m chosen from the measure: 20 m gave x1.33 from the slots.

New runtime range by size (`NativeExpeditionCityKit.Range`; what glows to the fog's end, other parts 80 + 25 L m, detail 50 + 25 L m up to 110 m), squared once per map. ## 2026-10-20 — Astra: reduce allocation spikes from stacked chip effects

- Branch/base: `codex/unity-chip-effect-perf`, shared/builder `ac94d722`. Owner requested fixes and test update publication.
- Replace eight hot `ToArray()` iteration sites in projectiles, chip explosions, persistent fields and vampire dash with pooled snapshots. Each foreach rents its own buffer; recursive blasts cannot overwrite an outer iteration. Preserve snapshot order/membership and next-tick fragment processing. Dispose clears object references and returns buffers on normal, early and exceptional exits.
- Skip the entire enemy snapshot/scan for non-damaging or healing fields, where every iteration previously did nothing. No damage, cooldown, collision, projectile limits, RNG, network schema or visual changes.
- Focused managed checks PASS: mutations, deferred spawns, nested same-type effects, empty input, oversized pool buffers, early exits and exception cleanup. Warm 1,000 x 300-object snapshots: original 2,424,000 allocated bytes; pooled exercise (including nested early exits) 0 bytes. This is an allocation microbenchmark, not an FPS or Unity/Mono claim.
- Full managed regression and pinned Unity Player/Runtime/Editor compilation are running; hosted/native builder gates and publication pending. Existing Windows combat gates remain required. No Windows GPU or multiplayer playtest performed here.
- Claude follow-up: renderer already batches dynamic meshes; profile mesh rebuild/sort and transparency under dense overlapping impacts before changing VFX. This patch addresses simulation allocation only; remaining whole-world scans and projectile membership searches are unchanged.

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: zombies no longer twitch toward the pilot under fire (merged into shared)

- **Branch/base:** `claude/zombie-twitch-fix`, from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` at `f930684`. Shared `ce9e02f` (Astra's #290 and `claude/zombie-black-fix`) merged in at `ef88bae`, and `f99b56f` (`claude/zombie-wound-fix`) at `6832650`. Implementation `9163d5f`. Presentation only. Merged into shared and the builder; not published.
- **Owner report:** "their movement still seems too fast (Not talking about their movement speed, rather their animations, they look like they're 'twitching' towards the player)". The recording is of Central Station: a pistol fired at shamblers running at the pilot. 18 of its 131 frames repeat.
- **Measured causes.** A scratch lab emulated `StepPveHordeCore`, `HitPveAdd` and `StructureNavMoveCore` at 60 Hz on the real `expedition-transit` nav, and presented the add through the real Core code (host 144 fps on Unity's interpolated transform, 20 Hz guest, 30 fps). The pistol's 23 damage is a quarter of a shambler's or runner's health, so every hit is an authority stagger (.45 s stop) plus a 2.2 m/s knock-back. Ranked by the effect of removing each cause (shambler under fire, head and chest world turn rate while it chases):
  1. The stagger's knockback reel started over on every hit: back to its start, in again within 54 ms, played at 2x its capture's pace. Without it, head p95 23.2 → 14.9 rad/s, p50 8.2 → 4.2, chest 10.2 → 5.2.
  2. The stagger ends with an instant 3.4 m/s restart, and the take crossed from standing to the chase in 2–3 frames. Head max 55 → 22 once the blend was rate-limited.
  3. The hurt sag (head droop, hunch, loose-head gain) stepped with the health at each hit. Head max 22 → 12 once eased.
  4. The station's nav is a 1 m grid with four links a node, and the Unity maps' empty `hazards` array keeps `StructureNavMoveCore` off its straight line. The authority's facing therefore snaps up to 59° two to four times a second. Facing p95 3.0 rad/s against 0 on a straight chase.
  5. Smaller onsets: hit envelopes started at full speed, the head snap landed in one frame, the head's lag read the root's acceleration at up to 9 m/s², and the twitch and tics ramped in 40–60 ms.
- **Not offenders:**
  - The cadence: 3.8 and 4.5–4.7 steps/s running, which fits Froude scaling for the 0.5 m legs. Unchanged.
  - The host's interpolated transform: 2 mm.
  - More root smoothing: tried and rejected. It costs 18 cm off the hit volume for a third less acceleration.
  - Walking a backward slide as stagger steps: tried and rejected, head p95 10.9 → 12.3.
- **Fix (Core only):**
  - `NativeHordeReact.Stumble`: staggers are links eased in over .16 s and out over .38 s, scaled by the hit's weight (a pistol .5, a step .75, heavy 1). Overlapping links are one stumble with the largest link's weight. The knockback take plays at its own pace from the stumble's start and holds at .42 s. It is a pure function of the hits and the clock. The gait's reel take and the trunk and arms read it.
  - The hit envelope rises from rest to the same peak and falls as before.
  - `NativeHordeGait.MoveSlew` (3/s): the upright kinds' stand-to-move take blend.
  - `HurtHalfLife` (.2 s): the health the sag reads.
  - `LifeAccelEase`/`LifeAccelMost` (.06 s, 5 m/s²): the head, chest and hands' lag input.
  - `HitSpread` (.035 s): the hit snap's impulse is fed in over a few frames.
  - The twitch and tics are eased in (.14 s, .1 s).
  - `HordeFlow.HeadingTau` (.26 s) through a new `BossRootFollow.HeadingTau`: the travelling facing's goal is eased. It is off through a wind-up, and off for every boss (default 0).
  - Files: `NativeHordeReact.cs`, `NativeHordeMotion.cs`, `NativeHordeLife.cs`, `NativeHordeFlow.cs`, `NativeBossMotionFollow.cs`. Tests: new `ZombieTwitchChecks.cs` (`--zombie-twitch`, also in `--zombie-loco`, `--zombie-flow` and the full run) and `Program.cs`. Docs: `ZOMBIE-LOCOMOTION.md` "Twitching under fire".
- **Results (lab, base → now; head p50/p95/max rad/s):**
  - Shambler under pistol fire, host 144: 8.2/23.2/64.8 → 3.0/6.8/10.3. Chest p95 10.2 → 3.5. Upper joints 12.0 → 3.2. The largest one-frame joint turn near a hit 0.43 → 0.12 rad.
  - Runner under fire: 24.5 → 7.4 p95, 59.8 → 13.8 max.
  - 20 Hz guest under fire: 23.1 → 6.8.
  - 30 fps under fire: 19.2 → 6.2.
  - Plain chase on the grid route: facing p95 2.99 → 1.64 (runner 3.89 → 1.99), head p95 6.0 → 4.7.
  - The brute, the bloater, the Hulk and the four station kinds measured equal or better.
  - Unchanged: the drawn root's acceleration under fire (84 m/s² p95, the authority's), its distance from the body (11.6 cm p95), the step rate and the cadence.
- **Animation impact:** none on hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement or networking.
  - The contact frame still lands within a frame of `LastAttack + strike`, including a blow started as a stumble lets go.
  - Posed bodies stay inside their hit volumes (`HordeKindChecks`).
  - No authority, rules, nav or wire file is in the diff.
  - The drawn facing can trail the authority's by about 6° on a grid route. The effects keep the authority's yaw.
  - Guests and the killcam derive everything from the replicated hits, the clock and the presented root, as before.
- **Checks (actual):**

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: zombie wounds on the drawn body, not on joint capsules (merged into shared)

- **Branch/base:** `claude/zombie-wound-fix` from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` at `f930684`, with shared `ce9e02f` (Astra's #290 and `claude/zombie-black-fix`) merged in at `1e4e99b`. Implementation `53b3a4e`; the DEV preview's vector type `85f0b67`. Presentation only. Merged into shared and the builder; not published.
- **Owner report:** "Zombie wounds appear off their body (Happens to other zombies as well)". The Central Station recording (pistol) shows dark-red strips crossing as X's above and beside the big kinds' heads.
- **Root cause.** It is in Core, which Unity and the managed checks share; it is not a Unity-only conversion:
  1. `NativeHordeGore.Place` (`Core/NativeHordeGore.cs` lines 191–208 at `f930684`) put every wound on a capsule round its joint (`SegmentRadius × Girth(kind) × drawn scale`), never on the model. The head's capsule ran 0.3 rig-m above the joint (`TipOf`) and took the limb girth (brute 1.45, Hulk 1.6), although the big kinds' heads are narrow (`HeadWidth` 0.74 and 0.6). The Hulk's head capsule is 0.43 m against a drawn head of at most 0.24 m, the brute's 0.22 m against 0.18 m. Other parts were fatter or thinner than their capsules too.
  2. `DrawWounds` (lines 609–611) drew the blood run as one straight strip in the wound's plane, moved down but laid along the frame's `b` axis, across the shot (median 51° off the surface's down), up to 5.6 wound sizes long. It stood off curved parts, and neighbouring runs crossed as X's.
  - **The matrices are not the cause.** `GoreN` is an exact transpose. Unity's `localToWorldMatrix` chain converts to exactly the matrices the checks pose (new check). The old "worst 0.4 cm from the hit" measured the wound centre against the same capsules, never the drawn pieces against the model.
  - `8740ceb`, `263cac2` and `f930684` measure identically.
- **Measured.** Each drawn wound piece's farthest corner from its own drawn part, with ZombieLit's per-add proportions and missing pieces applied. The scratch probe covered all 16 kinds (look 0) with 13 aims, 4 causes and 3 facings, standing and walking, at 4 ages. Worst / p95, before → after:
  - shambler 26.5 / 13.2 → 2.4 / 1.3 cm; runner 24.9 / 13.2 → 2.0 / 1.2;
  - brute 31.7 / 14.4 → 2.1 / 1.4; spitter 21.5 / 12.3 → 2.3 / 1.3;
  - crawler 24.9 / 14.4 → 1.7 / 1.2; bloater 29.8 / 16.5 → 1.9 / 1.4;
  - Hulk 55.3 / 36.1 → 3.5 / 2.6;
  - the nine zone kinds 17.9–41.4 / 7.7–21.5 → 1.8–2.5 / 1.2–1.8.
  - Wound centres, p95: 3.5–22.6 cm → 0.0.
- **Fix:**
  - New `Core/NativeHordeGoreBody.cs` holds each joint's triangles of the kind's look at the Full tier, in the joint's own frame, with the add's proportions and missing pieces applied. It answers ray, nearest-point and near queries. The bank hands it the Full models it builds (31 bodies, 5.9 MB).
  - `NativeHordeGore.PlaceOn`: the wound goes on the first drawn part the shot's ray enters. The ray is a projectile's own 3D travel (`e.Normal`, its velocity), within the authority's part. If the ray only grazed the authority's capsule, the wound goes on the nearest drawn point.
  - `NativeHordeGoreState.OnBody` fits the footprint to the part, down to 0.38 of its size. It traces the run down the surface at the hit in three snapped steps. `DrawWounds` draws each stretch along itself, and drips leave the run's tip.
  - `ShownJoints`: a lost limb is never wounded, on any frame, because `Lost` is the replicated `Pve.Lost`.
  - `FromColumns` and `Column` hold the Unity joint conversion in Core.
  - Runtime, `NativeHordeGorePresentation.cs`:
    - `GoreN`/`GoreU` go through Core;
    - the hit carries `Shot` and `Look`;
    - a live add's wounds draw only while it is on the Full model, which matters only at the edge of the nearest-24 ranking.
  - Also changed: `NativeHordeGoreGallery.cs` (`Look`, `Shot`). Minimal edits to shared files: `NativeHordeKindModels.cs` gains one line (`NativeHordeGoreBody.Keep(built)` for the Full tier), and `NativeHordeKindPresentation.cs` gains one argument (`GoreWoundsJob(m.Id,rig,s.Tier)`).
  - Not touched: `NativeZombieLit.shader`, the colours, and the pose code.
- **Animation impact:** none on hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement or networking. The poses are read only through the rig's joint matrices.
- **Checks (actual):**
  - `--zombie-gore`, Release and Debug: PASS, 315,398 zombie-gore checks (14 PASS lines), digest `0xf8a1621b9ac8bba8` in both.
  - New `OnBody` group, against the test's own drawn body (the shader's vert written out, not `NativeHordeGoreBody`): 1,106 hits on all 16 kinds and every look, walking and standing, 5 causes, 3 gore tiers, 17,032 pieces. Worst 3.7 cm (a Hulk piece); 95 % within 1.6 cm (wound), 0.8 cm (run) and 1.5 cm (drop); centres on the part.

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: zombies near-black at Central Station: the station now lights bodies with its practical slots (merged into shared)

- **Branch/base:** `claude/zombie-black-fix`, from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` at `f930684`. Presentation only. Implementation commit `ffcaf05`. Merged into shared and the builder; not published.
- **Owner report:** "Seems the zombies are appearing almost completely black a lot of the time?" This was in the Windows build, Expedition, Central Station. The owner added: "The glowing eyes are still fine". In the recording, the bodies are about 4–5/255 next to a floor at about 100/255.
- **Root cause (from the code):**
  - The project is Built-in and Linear: no SRP package, `m_ColorSpace: 1`.
  - The station's practical lights are not Unity lights. `StationScenery` gives the eight that matter to the camera to `NativeLighting.PickedLights`. These go to `NativeBlockLit`'s own light block (`NativeBlockLit.shader:602`, `BlockLights`), so they light the floor, the walls and the kit.
  - `ZombieLit` adds those same slots only while the global `_ArenaActorLit` is on (`NativeZombieLit.shader:187`, `NativeWardLight.cginc` `ActorLights`). `SourceLit` (pilots) does the same.
  - `NativeLighting.Apply` turns the switch off for every map (`NativeLighting.cs:232`). Ward Zero (`NativeWardZeroPresentation.cs:255`) and the Ironworks (`NativeIronworksPresentation.cs:253`) turn it on every frame. The station never did. The station boss (THE 6:47) set it on its own material only (`NativeStationBossPresentation.cs:232`).
  - So a station zombie had only Unity's lights:
    - the `central-station` look's moon key (.5, soft shadows at strength .9 under the roofs and the vault's glazing);
    - a .14 rim;
    - a trilight ambient of about .001 (scales .085/.065/.055).
  - That puts the skin at about 3/255 and the suit at 0.
  - The first-person gun is drawn by the view-model camera, which only draws layer 10 (`ConversionGame.cs:79`). That is why the roof does not shadow it.
  - **Why it showed after 10-19:** the gore pass took off the glowing seams, cracks and accents, the rising flow and the lavender rim. That cut the bodies' emission by about 60% (emissive area 0.25 → 0.065 m² over the seven kinds' first looks), and at the station the emission was all that carried them.
  - **Albedo is not the cause.** Against `dab15f3` the skin moved -6% and the suit -8% in luminance (the stain). Vertex colours are linear and go to the shader raw, with no double sRGB conversion. They are uploaded. The shader keeps Unity's ambient, vertex lights, add pass and shadows.
- **Fix:** `Runtime/NativeExpeditionStationPresentation.cs` now calls `NativeLighting.ActorLights(true)` every frame in `StationScenery`. The call comes after the map gate and the slot pick, and outside the eye test, so the killcam gets it too. This is the same as the Ironworks.
  - No change to shaders, models, colours, rules, timing, hitboxes or networking. No allocation: two global writes by cached id.
  - The eyes are emission and are unchanged.
  - Bodies take the lamps the floor takes and stay dark where the floor is dark, so the moody look and the grime and blood remain.
  - No readability floor (extra ambient or rim): the emulation already puts bodies at the floor's light, and an extra floor would make them glow in an unlit station.
  - Also affected at the station: pilots, the station's kinds and the view-model gun now take the slots, as on Ward Zero and the Ironworks.
- **Checks (actual):**
  - New `Tests/ZombieLightChecks.cs`: `--zombie-light`, also in `--station-visuals` and the full run, 64 checks. It covers:
    - the contract: `ZombieLit`'s pragma and passes, its lighting and surf lines as emulated, the hook and the wrap, `NativeLighting.ActorLights`, and the switch in the station, Ironworks and Ward Zero;
    - every look with practicals whose body base is under .02 lights its bodies. Only `quarantine` .003, `central-station` .0055 and `ironworks` .0095 qualify. The town and the arenas read by their own fill;
    - an albedo floor: skin .171, suit .028;
    - the station emulated at 4,808 walkable nodes, key in shadow. The floor median is 29/255. Skin is 27/255 with actor lights against 3/255 before. The median skin/floor ratio is .67. Under lamps, skin is 41/255 and suit 12/255, and the skin is greener than the suit. Nothing allocates.
  - Mutations: removing the station's call fails the contract. Skipping the contract leaves skin at 3/255 and fails the emulation. A darkened town look fails the dark-look rule.
  - Groups rc 0: `--zombie-light`, `--station-visuals`, `--zombie-gore`, `--ward-lighting`, `--ironworks-visuals`, `--station-enemies`, `--station-boss-presentation`.
  - run5b on the branch's code (`ffcaf05` plus this docs commit, before this line was filled in), rc1–rc5 all 0: Unity Runtime and Editor compile; relay and managed suite with 809 PASS lines, 0 FAIL (the new zombie light line included); 140 Python tests (1 skipped); package; diff-check.
  - After merging shared `6828647` (#290, Astra's Expedition death input fix) without a rebase: run5b again on the merged tree, rc1–rc5 all 0, 809 PASS, 0 FAIL. The groups above pass again, plus `--dev-tools` and `--expedition-pick`.
- **Renders:** a scratch CPU emulation, not in git (`renders-zombie-black/`). It runs ZombieLit's and NativeBlockLit's maths with the live look, kit and picked slots, in the concourse, ticket hall and P2, before and after. The ticket hall's before frame is close to the recording: floor 77/255 against about 100, bodies 6/255 against 4–5. Not emulated: shadow maps (the key is shadowed everywhere), the kit and walls, shafts, haze, bloom and post.
- **Not run:** Unity Editor or Windows play (not available here), so the look in the engine and its per-frame cost are unverified.
- **Risks:**

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: zombie gore bound to the authority hit metadata (merged into shared)

- **Branch/base:** `claude/zombie-gore-bind`, from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` at `8740ceb` (Astra's PR #289 `codex/zombie-gore-state` merged). Presentation only. Implementation commit `da3f812`. Merged into shared and the builder; not published.
- **Bound, per the contract in `docs/ZOMBIE-GORE.md` ("Authority hit metadata", new "Binding" table):**
  - `Head` (with `HasHordeHit`) decides the head on its own. It puts the wound on the head even when the torso's share was larger, and gives the cavity spray, the head's bits, the death's head burst and the existing headshot head snap (`NativeHordeReact`, 2.2x). `Head` false means no head hit, even when the nearest drawn part is the head.
  - `HasPart`/`Part` place the wound at the nearest point of the drawn joints that make up that part (`NativeHordeGore.PartJoints`). The map is the severed-limb gore's own (even bits on the rig's left). The checks confirm it against the authority's `NativeHordeDamage.Part` on posed bodies. Part 0 with `HasPart` is a known torso; with `HasPart` false the nearest drawn part is kept.
  - **Lost parts:** the authority names the part before moving the damage to the torso, and a lost part is not drawn. The wound goes on what is left of the limb: the upper arm under a lost forearm, the thigh under a lost shin. Otherwise it goes on the trunk (a lost head: the neck). It never lands on a hidden joint. The lost bits are the replicated `Pve.Lost`; for the killing blow, the last ones the add was drawn with.
  - `Raw`: the hit's strength is the larger of `Raw` and `Amount`. It drives the gib (80 % of max HP, heavy round or heavy blow), the head burst (50 %, not an arrow), the spray's severity and the burst's power. Blasts and crushes keep `Amount`, because a blast's `Raw` is its centre damage before the shares' falloff. `Raw - Amount` is never used.
  - Old frames (`HasHordeHit` false) read none of these fields and draw bit for bit as before.
- **Files:**
  - Core `NativeHordeGore.cs`: `Strength`, the part tables and `Struck`, a joint mask for `Place`, the `GoreHit` fields and `Hit`.
  - Runtime `NativeHordeGorePresentation.cs` (`HordeGoreHit`) and `NativeHordeKindPresentation.cs` (the head flag for the reaction).
  - Tests `ZombieGoreChecks.cs`; docs `ZOMBIE-GORE.md`.
- **Animation impact:** none on hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement or networking. The only motion change is that the existing head-snap strength also follows `Head`. No authority, rules, network or wire file is in the diff (checked with `git diff` against shared).

  - The new metadata checks cover: present vs absent (and stray fields ignored without `HasHordeHit`); the head flag over a torso-largest share; every LIMB bit on four kinds at four facings; the authority's `NativeHordeDamage.Part` against the drawn body (125 limb hits agree on the side, 126 of 160 on the exact part); known torso vs unknown part; all 162 closed sets of lost limbs; the raw gib, head-burst and blast thresholds; spray and burst strength; host/guest/killcam with the metadata; zero allocation with metadata hits.
  - Mutation runs, by hand and not kept: left/right swapped, raw ignored, lost parts ignored, the head flag ignored, blast raw used, the old path altered, and the test's authority frame unmirrored. Each made `--zombie-gore` fail.

- **Renders:** offline WebGL emulation, not Unity; scratch only, not in git. A forearm hit placed by `Part` vs inferred, and a rifle overkill (clamped corpse vs `Raw` gib).

## 2026-10-20 — Claude: allocation checks read bytes a background GC added (CI fix, merged into shared)

- **Branch:** `claude/alloc-check-bgc`, from shared `claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` at `f94fa98`. Test project only; no game, Runtime or Core change. Merged into shared and the builder; not published.
- **Failure:** PR #62 `native-source` at `f94fa98` failed `SpawnInChecks.Allocation`: "12000 frames ... allocate nothing (8088 bytes)". The same run passes locally, and the code allocates nothing. Earlier one-off reds of the same kind include `ChipSelectChecks` 1856 bytes (boss-vfx merge check, 2026-10-19) and the 680/5328/5024 bytes noted in `CoreTests.csproj` (2026-10-15).
- **Root cause (.NET 8 `gc.cpp`):** at the end of a background (concurrent) gen2 collection's mark phase, `background_mark_phase` calls `repair_allocation_contexts(FALSE)`, which runs `void_allocation`. That zeroes every thread's `alloc_ptr`/`alloc_limit` without taking the unused tail off `alloc_bytes`. `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` is `alloc_bytes - (alloc_limit - alloc_ptr)`, so it jumps by the tail, up to one 8 KB quantum the thread never allocated. Blocking collections retire contexts through `fix_allocation_context(..., for_gc_p=TRUE)`, which subtracts the tail. The checks' own buffers (the spawn-in sink is 3.3 MB of large-object arrays) can start a background gen2 just before a measured loop; its mark phase then ends inside the loop.
- **Evidence:** a probe ran `SpawnInChecks.Allocation` 1500 times with tiering off (as CI), with a thread churning gen0/gen1 garbage.
  - Concurrent GC on: 6/1500 failures (8088 ×5, 3056), each with a gen2 collection inside the run.
  - `DOTNET_gcConcurrent=0`: 0/1500.
  - Without the noise thread: 0/1500 either way.
  - A plain 2M-iteration loop under gen0-only noise: 0/200. A copy of the loop instrumented around each call never failed.
- **Fix:** `Tests/CoreTests.csproj` sets `<ConcurrentGarbageCollection>false</ConcurrentGarbageCollection>` (runtimeconfig `System.GC.Concurrent: false`), with the cause in a comment next to `TieredCompilation`. All 189 measurement sites keep their exact `== 0` checks; none is relaxed, retried or skipped. The game is unaffected (Unity runs its own GC).
- **Checks (actual):** run5b on the merged shared head (this fix plus `claude/rounds-state-bind`), rc1–rc5 all 0: Unity Runtime and Editor compile; relay and managed suite with 807 PASS lines, every allocation check at `== 0` under blocking GC; 140 Python tests (1 skipped); package; diff-check. Worst melee split 7 ms (limit 400).
- **Risk:** gen2 collections in the test process now pause the test thread. The only wall-clock assertions are the bisect splits (< 400 ms). Not tested: a CI runner, until this push.

- **Root causes (measured on an offline harness):** it runs the Core code against an emulated 60 Hz authority with the crowd's separation, a 20 Hz network and 144 fps frames, and renders the built voxel meshes.
  - **Rapid back and forth.**
    - The pack's walks and chases were captured at 0.12 to 0.54 rig m/s. `NativeZombieMotion.Rate` played them at 2 to 2.8 times their pace to keep up with the authority's 1.1 to 1.6 m/s walks, so whole bodies were time-compressed.
    - The walkers took 3.4 to 4.4 steps a second and the runs 5 to 6.9. The upper joints turned at 4.2 to 6.7 rad/s p95. The hands' jerk was 24,000 to 58,000 m/s³, with about half their motion above 4 Hz (shambler 54 %).
    - In crowds, the separation jostle (±0.23 m/s, up to ±0.63) flipped the walk-to-run blend through a 0.08 s spring.
  - **Arms detach.** The zombie chests are narrower than the rig's clavicles (±0.275). The shoulder blocks start at the clavicle, so the shoulder and arm hung 2 to 10 cm off the torso at rest, on 17 looks across 9 kinds (measured on the built meshes with the per-add proportions). The capture's shoulder motion widened the gap.
- **Changes:**
  - New `Core/NativeHordeLoco.cs` (a partial of `NativeHordeGait`):

    - `GaitSpeedStep`: a gait speed eased with a 0.18 s half-life, the run blend's slew limited to 2.2/s, and a setting-off hysteresis at 0.24 and 0.14 m/s.

## 2026-10-19 — Claude: permanent account XP, presentation side and proposed contract (merged into shared, unbound)

- **Branch:** `claude/account-xp-presentation`, based on shared `6bf4896` (`claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv`). Presentation only. Merged into shared and the builder (unbound: players see no change); not published. The contract is proposed and awaits Astra; nothing is bound.
- **Owner request (2026-10-19), summarised:**
  - start the presentation side of permanent account XP (PvP and PvE completions, mainly from active playtime and objectives);
  - a post-match XP panel (previous level and progress, the earned breakdown, the new progress with a level-up animation);
  - a compact level in the main menu;
  - pending, confirmed and failed (with retry) states;
  - DEV fixtures with mock values.
  The presentation must not calculate rewards, choose the curve, write account XP or grant unlocks. Animate each confirmed completion once and never show pending as saved. Keep XP apart from chips and currency, and propose the contract before wiring.
- **Contract (proposed v1):** `docs/ACCOUNT-XP-PRESENTATION.md`, Core `NativeAccountXp.cs`.
  - `AccountXpAward`:
    - identity and state: `version`, `completionId`, `account`, `mode`, `status` (pending, confirmed or failed), `revision`;
    - numbers: `lines[] {key,label,xp}`, `previousTotal`, `newTotal`, `previousLevel`, `newLevel`, `bands[] {level,start,next}`;
    - failure: `attempt`, `retry` (auto, manual, later or none), `retryIn`, `reason`.
  - `AccountXpSummary`: `known`, `total`, `level`, `levelStart`, `nextLevelAt`, `pending`.
  - The same `completionId` is re-issued pending → confirmed (or failed → pending → confirmed), its `revision` rising.
  - Every number is the authority's. The panel only interpolates inside the supplied bands.
  - Validation degrades instead of guessing:
    - an invalid id, status or version, or another account's award, is not shown;
    - inconsistent totals show "details unavailable";
    - bad bands show the numbers without a bar;
    - a line sum ≠ the totals is shown as given and flagged in DEV.
- **What it shows:**
  - **PvP match end and PvE results:** an XP panel in its own column beside the results, the pair centred. The results narrow to make room (never below 480 / 420) and keep their old place when there is no award.
  - **Expedition:** a card over the J screen. It opens by itself on a new completion's award and again at its confirmation; the footer's ACCOUNT XP button reopens it.
  - **Home:** a third nameplate line: an XP hexagon with the level, LEVEL n, a thin saved-progress bar and PENDING.
  - **Pending:** a hatched ghost gain, "CONFIRMING REWARD…" and "Not saved to your account yet."
  - **Failed:** the authority's reason with RETRYING IN n s, TRY AGAIN, WILL RETRY WHEN YOU'RE BACK ONLINE or THIS REWARD WAS NOT SAVED; the gain is a red ghost marked NOT SAVED.
  - **Confirmed:** the lines lock in, the bar fills band by band with a pop, burst and flash at every threshold (chained for several levels; 32 or more collapse into one "LEVEL UP ×n"), then SAVED TO YOUR ACCOUNT.
  - **Separation:** XP has its own ultraviolet tone and its own words, never the wallet's gold, the chips' cyan, $ or chips.
- **Animate once:** the first sight of a confirmed completion animates, and the completion is written to a local record at once.
  - The record is `account-xp-celebrated-v1.txt` in the user data folder: the newest 200 keys (account and completionId). It is UI state only and DEV mock ids are never written.

## 2026-10-18 — Claude: party loading indicator on the stage loading screen (merged into shared)

- **Branch:** `claude/party-loading-indicator`, based on shared `e13e610` (#276). Presentation only; merged into shared, not published.
- **Owner request:** "Also, lets add a loading indicator for players (When starting expeditions, so we can see where each player is on loading screen)".
- **What it shows:** for an Expedition start or area load, a party panel under the loading screen's title block (Core `NativePartyLoading.cs`; Runtime `NativePartyLoadingHud`, `NativePartyLoadingUI`):
  - Header: PARTY · n and READY k / n. Footer: WAITING FOR n PLAYERS… while anyone in this load is still loading, then EVERYONE'S IN.
  - One row per member: YOU first, then this load's members by seat, then everyone else. Each row has the weapon icon, the name (YOU or HOST), a chip (WAITING, LOADING, READY, IN WORLD, DROPPED, EXTRACTED) and a bar.
  - Bars: mine is my real load (the screen's shown progress). Others show an indeterminate sweep while loading, then fill and tick when they arrive. A dashed track means dropped.
  - Motion: rows rise in on a CSS curve, staggered. Reduced effects: no rise, sweep, fill or pop. No per-frame allocation.
  - Layout: fits 720p @1.5 (compact rows, two columns from five members) through 3440×1440 and 4K, for 1–8 rows. The scan and the foot are unchanged. Expedition parties are capped at 4 (`NativeExpeditionParty.Capacity`); 8 is the room and view maximum.
- **What drives each state (from the code):** no per-member load progress or readiness is replicated today.
  - The view carries `members[]` (connected, extracted, area, pendingArea) and `areaBarrier` (active, target, ready of required: counts, no names).
  - A loading guest receives the view at most every 5 s (Astra's bootstrap budget).
  - DROPPED is `!connected`; EXTRACTED is `extracted`.
  - First load or new loop (barrier target is the city, nothing entered): each client's barrier counts only itself. Every other member shows LOADING with no value, on the host and guests alike, so a guest cannot see that the host is already in the world.
  - Area transfer: the cohort is every member whose pendingArea is my destination. They stay LOADING until the authority's count covers every other cohort member (READY), and show IN WORLD after the commit.
    - A partial count names nobody: the rows stay LOADING, while the header and footer follow the count.
    - My own report is taken off the count once I am locally ready, so no one is shown in early.
  - A member already in the destination is IN WORLD and counted. Members elsewhere show IN WORLD at their place (or LOADING into their own pendingArea), dimmed and not counted.
  - Me: LOADING with my real progress, READY when my presentation is ready while the barrier holds, then IN WORLD.
  - WAITING comes only from a replicated `loadState` (none today). A guest waits for the host's build in the lobby (status "Host is loading Expedition…"); its loading screen covers when its first frame arrives. That flow is unchanged.
- **PvP/PvE:** not shown there. The stage gate sends only Ready of Required; per-seat readiness stays in the host's `NativeStageBarrier`. The pilots' pips stay.
- **Shared files (small hooks):**
  - `NativeStageLoading.cs`: `Measure(..., party)`, plus `Roster` and `TagHidden`.
  - `NativeStageLoadingHud.cs`: the roster parameter; the title block honours the panel's room.
  - `NativeStageLoadingUI.cs`: one call.
  - `Tests/Program.cs`: the run line and `--party-loading`.
- **For Astra (contract, not implemented):**
  1. Client to host: `expedition-load-progress {epoch, areaIdentity, loadProgress}`.
     - The value comes from `ConversionGame.StageLoadProgress`: 0..1 while the loading screen is up, 1 once the stage's presentation is ready, -1 when no load is shown.
     - Send while that member's ticket is not Ready, at most 4/s (≥0.25 s apart), only on a change of ≥0.02 or after 1 s, with a final 1.0.
     - The host sets its own value locally.
  2. Host validation:
     - The sender comes from the verified peer seat, and `areaIdentity` must match the member's current ticket.
     - The value must be finite; clamp it to 0..1 and never let it go down within one ticket.
     - Drop anything over 4/s, and ignore reports once the member is Ready.
  3. Relay in `ExpeditionViewMember`: `public float loadProgress=-1;` and `public string loadState;`.
     - `loadState`: "waiting" (ticket issued, no report yet), "loading" (reports arriving, not Ready), "ready" (Ready, cohort still pending), "world" (Ready, no pending), "dropped" (disconnected or the load window expired). Null or "" means unknown (an older host).
     - `loadProgress`: 0..1 for the current ticket (1 when Ready), -1 unknown. JsonUtility leaves an absent float at 0, so the adapter trusts `loadProgress` only when `loadState` is set.
     - Add both to the managed codec and its validation (finite, -1 or 0..1, the five words).
  4. Carrier: the public view reaches loading guests only every 5 s. While anyone is loading, also send a small `expedition-party-load {run, epoch, members:[{account, loadProgress, loadState}]}` (≤4 entries) to every connected member at ≤4 Hz. The receiver writes it into its current view's members.
  5. Binding: `NativePartyLoadModel.ReplicatedProgress` and `ReplicatedState` are one line each (the bodies are in their summaries). Until then both return -1 and unknown. `PartyLoadingChecks` then requires the binding (a reflection tripwire).
  - Optional: an `ExpeditionStartPending` flag (set by `expedition-starting`, cleared by the first view or a lobby at the same epoch) would let a guest's loading screen cover while the host builds, showing WAITING.
- **Checks (run5b, all five steps exit 0):**
  - Unity 6000.3.24f1 Runtime and Editor compile OK.
  - Relay: 787 PASS, including the new `PartyLoadingChecks` (`--party-loading`, 3,601 checks) and `TransitionLoadingChecks` (3,613).
    - The new checks cover the state per source, YOU first, the footer counts, the adapters at -1 today, and layouts at 1280×720 @1.5, 1920×1080, 3440×1440 and 3840×2160 for 1–8 members plus eight more resolutions and UI scales.
    - They also cover the reduced tier, zero per-frame allocation, and scans showing that the authority and network files do not touch the panel.
  - Python: 140 OK (1 skipped). Package OK. Diff-check OK.
  - After the run, one doc comment in `NativeStageLoadingHud.cs` was rewrapped; the Runtime compile was rerun and passed.
- **Not run:** Unity Editor play, Windows, two-client host/guest loads, real load timing. The renders are offline IMGUI emulation (scratchpad `renders-party-loading`). The "contract bound" renders use the checks' stand-in states.
- **Risks:**
  - Until Astra binds the contract, the first load shows every other member as LOADING (a guest sees the host loading even when the host is in the city).
  - The transfer count reaches a loading guest only every 5 s.
  - The panel is not on the Expedition transfer screen that remains after the loading screen's 20 s hold.
  - A solo load reads WAITING FOR 1 PLAYER… (the owner's wording, counting me).
- **Animation impact:** none on hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement or networking.

## 2026-10-18 — Claude: last enemies of a kill quota marked (merged into shared)

- Branch `claude/quota-last-markers`, base shared `e13e610` (PR #276 merged). Merged into shared and the builder, no PR, nothing
  published. Owner (2026-10-18): "We need some kind of indicator for the last enemies of a quota (Like maybe last 5?) In case
  they get stuck so players know where to find them."
- **What (presentation only):** `Core/NativeQuotaMarks.cs` holds every rule; `Runtime/NativeQuotaMarksPresentation.cs` draws;
  `Runtime/NativeQuotaMarkAudio.cs` pings. Details in `docs/EXPEDITION-PRESENTATION.md` "Quota markers (the last enemies)".
  - Trigger: 1–5 kills left (`NativeQuotaMarks.Threshold`) in the viewer's current instance (`instances[].current`,
    `target - progress`), not cleared, no boss (`bosses[]` empty, no `bossArrivals[]` entry for the area). Off at 0, in the
    boss phase, outside the area, while loading or frozen. Ward Zero, Central Station and City Ironworks all use these fields,
    so one rule covers all three (checked on the real split-area run for each).
  - Which: live hostile horde adds of the presented arena (a split area's arena holds only its own), the 8 nearest (`Cap`);
    never corpses, hub/town zombies, the zone boss or its summons, DEV monsters or adds still queued at an entry. Positions are
    the adds' presented roots (new read-only `ArenaPresentation.HordeDrawnRoot`), so guests mark what they draw.
  - Marker: a downward kite 0.6 m over the kind's head (Hulk: 3.66 m above the floor), drawn over the scene (walls never hide
    it), metres label, 28→15 UI px from 6 to 48 m, 1.2 s pulse; hidden within 4 m while in plain sight (camera ray through
    `NativeArena.WorldMask`), .55 over the crosshair; a farther marker lined up behind a nearer one is lifted clear above it. Colour: the HUD's enemy tone Danger `#ff4d6d` (not hazard amber, not ally
    cyan). Deviation: an IMGUI overlay anchored to the world point (on top by construction) instead of a depth-test-off world
    mesh, so the label stays crisp and no shader is needed.
  - Off screen / behind: edge darts with the distance on a rounded rectangle inset from the edges (clear of the objective and
    LAST tags and the cooldown cards); behind the camera they lean to the bottom; close ones are spread apart.
  - HUD: `LAST n · MARKED` under the objective tag, and under the J screen's KILL QUOTA bar.
  - Cue: one soft ping per quota (run, loop, area), not on count changes or on returning to the same quota; key
    `expedition.quota.mark` with a built-in synthesized ping as the fallback (never silent). Like the door keys, the key is not
    yet registered in `NativeSoundKeys`, so the bank cannot carry an owner clip until it is.
  - Tiers: Reduced effects no pulse or glow; low graphics no glow; no allocation per frame.

## 2026-10-17 — Claude: zombie motion pass (on branch, not merged)

- **Branch and status:** `claude/zombie-motion`, from shared `f3d8eb4`. Shared was merged in twice: `5dc860d` as `1cd0006`, then the newest, `03dddab`, as `fbc298c`. - **What changed** (presentation only; full write-up in `docs/ZOMBIE-MOTION.md`):
  - **Clock and root:** every horde add is posed on a continuous horde clock (`Core/NativeHordeFlow.cs`: `HordeClock`), never `arena.Time`. It is the replica render time on a guest and the visual clock on the host, it rides through stalls, and it slows near the newest frame. The drawn root (`HordeFlow`, on the boss library's `BossRootFollow`) follows a guest's own snapshots (new read-only accessor `Runtime/NativeReplicaFrames.cs`) or the host's 60 Hz body carried to the visual clock. Speed comes from that root; turning is rate- and acceleration-limited, with lean.
  - **Feet:** a landing beyond reach is planted where the leg reached, a trailing foot rolls onto its ball, an over-reached walking foot steps instead of sliding, each foot sets off on its own phase, steps are planned under the balanced hips, and the hips ease into a stride while planted feet stay in reach. Crawler legs no longer spin when folded shut.
  - **Secondary motion** (`Core/NativeHordeLife.cs`): loose head, dangling arms, trunk lag and sway, footfall dips, and per-seed loll, hunch, dead arm, limp and tics. Hurt adds sag, and the hinged jaws flap.
  - **Strikes:** they cock, accelerate into contact exactly at `LastAttack + strike`, follow through and settle. Consecutive blows cross-fade, a guest plays a blow out before the next, and a cancelled wind-up fades without ever reaching contact. Arm layers are solved per take, which removes wrist and elbow flips.
  - **Pop killer** (`Core/NativeHordeBlend.cs`, inertialization): it covers entrances, the drop's touchdown, kind swaps and the death hand-over, and catches arm and trunk pops. Legs and root are never held back.
  - **Drop fixes:** the leap no longer plays an unbuilt take, the slam is continuous, and the finished landing holds its take's last frame.
- **Affected systems:** `Core/NativeHordeMotion.cs`, `Core/NativeHordeReact.cs` (`NewestHit`), the new Core files above, and `Runtime/NativeHordeKindPresentation.cs` (pose and clock regions only: clock, flow, blend, attack hand-over, jaw flap, death blend). Tests: `ZombieFlowChecks.cs` (new), updates to `ZombieMotionChecks`, `HordeRoamChecks`, `HulkSpitterChecks` and `StationEnemyChecks`, and the seven `kindN.motion` lines of `station-enemies-baseline.txt`.

## 2026-10-16 — Claude: footsteps cycled through terrains on one surface (surface lookup, memory, one series per key)

- Owner: "walking continuously on one surface cycles through sounds that resemble different terrains." Trace the surface and key per foot contact; keep surfaces in separate pools; same check for zombies.
- Branch `claude/footstep-surface-fix`, base `origin/claude/sleepy-ritchie-g8ruhv` `e8de6fc`; implementation `3b2c9d4`; shared `930bf5d` (PRs #251, #252 and the join circle layout draft) merged in afterwards (`190ac4b`) (the probe moved to the arena's physics world, docs kept both sides). Fast-forwarded into shared and the builder after review (no PR, no live release); the new private bank `LocalAssets-footsteps-surfaces.zip` was sent to the owner.
- **Cause, with evidence.** Per-plant trace on the maps' own colliders (managed raycast of NativeArena's colliders, real gaits, the real banks' manifests and `NativeSoundBank.Next`):
  - The key was stable. On every 60 s route (Ward Zero hall, town, Ward Zero deck, factory catwalk; walk and sprint; gun, magic, bow, melee and no-gait routes) every plant classified one key, before and after.
  - The pools were mixed. `move.step.concrete` (Ward Zero, its instance, the town) held 4 `_Stones_Footsteps/FOOTSTEP_Stones_Run_01` takes and 4 `FOOTSTEP_Concrete_Walk_01`.
    - Measured: stones at 0.93-2.1 kHz spectral centroid, flatness .04-.25, 7-12 crunch transients; concrete at 0.22-0.31 kHz, flatness under .002, 2 transients.
    - Ward Zero hall: 281 walk plants played 141 stones and 140 concrete takes, with 160 series changes between consecutive plants (sprint: 442 plants, 256 changes). After: 0.
  - Metal mixed `Metal_Run_01/02/03`: 237 series changes in 281 plants on Ward Zero's deck. Snow mixed four series (a 0.36 kHz packed thud with 1.5-2.3 kHz crunches), wood three, gravel two.
  - The coordinator's capsule-centre premise did not hold. `NativeArena.cs` reports `a.Position=Vec(p.Body.position-Vector3.up*.865f)`, the feet. The old probe (feet +.4 to -.8 m) reached flat floors.
  - Real lookup gaps, fixed:
    - Stair and ramp wedges (no `NativePropBody`) fell to the map floor whatever their treads. Today's wedges are all stone, so no audible flip.
    - No hysteresis: a seam, a rail or a boundary could flip per plant. The probe sat under the body, not the planted foot.
    - A failed clip load fell through to a stand-in or built-in take, mixing another sound into a key with clips (`BankPlay` false).
    - Zombies were surface-blind: a shambler on a metal deck shuffled on asphalt.
- **Code** (presentation only):
  - `Core/NativeFootfalls.cs`: `NativeFootSurface` (probe start .4 m over the feet, reach to .8 m under, scaled over 1; key from hit material or map floor; zombie key by surface; leading-foot pick). `NativeSurfaceMemory`: first plant at once; a new surface on its second plant in a row; reset after 2.5 s (a Hulk steps every ~1.1 s), a rewind or a landing. `NativeFootfall` gains `FootX/FootZ/Scale`.
  - `Core/NativeSoundCues.cs`: step key constants.
  - `Runtime/NativeFootfallPresentation.cs`: a pilot's footfall carries the posed foot bone leading the travel (else its position); a zombie's its landed limb and scale.
  - `Runtime/NativeFootstepAudio.cs`: the Core probe at the planted foot, in the arena's own physics world (`arena.PhysicsWorld`, from Astra's area runtime #252, merged in). A hit names its `NativePropBody` material, else its collider's physics material (the wedges carry their treads'). The memory is per pilot and per add. Zombies: their gait keys on concrete and stone; the surface's `move.step.*` pool at their own pitch on metal, wood, gravel and snow. The crawler drags on every surface: a drag is body friction, unlike any footfall pool. A key with clips plays only its own takes.
  - `Runtime/NativeHulkChargeAudio.cs`: the charge warning's stomps use the same surface and memory.
- **Clips** (private bank; no audio committed). One recording series of the key's own surface per key, nearest the series' acoustic medoid:
  - concrete: 8 `Concrete_Walk_01` (RR02/04/06/07/09/10/11/12), was 4 stones + 4 concrete. Gravel: 6 `Gravel_Run_04`, was `Run_01`+`Run_04`.
  - metal: 6 `Metal_Run_02`, was `Run_01/02/03`. Snow: 6 `Snow_Run_04`, was `Run_01/02/04/05`. Wood: 6 `Wood_Run_01`, was `Run_01/02/03`. Stone: 6 Fantasy `Stone_Medium` A/B/C/D/G/J, was A/C/E/G.
  - Zombie shuffle: dropped RR3 and RR7. They are gritty (centroid 1.3-1.6 kHz, flatness .13-.16) and measure nearest snow. Run, heavy and crawl are unchanged.
  - The stones takes measure as gravel; they are dropped, so gravel stays one series.
  - Walk and sprint on one surface share one key; only rate and gain differ by gait.
  - Built with the bank's own chain (`fxbuild` = `tools/build_effects_audio.py`; scratch `fsurf/tools/build_surfaces.py`, `measure.py`, `select.py`). Every other file is byte-identical.
  - `scratchpad/LocalAssets-footsteps-surfaces.zip`: 12,741,728 bytes, sha256 `5465e1718b37fabe656610ffa9d8dd6801387c2529cfa4e2dff1aa11d5585268`. Installer `--check`: 226 keys, 593 clips, 13.14 MB. `LICENSES.md` and ASSET-CREDITS "Footstep surfaces" list every source.

  - Red stays on: the code reddens the screen only for damaging hits in the last 1.2 s. The HUD's under-attack alarm reads the same events and window and is absent in every recorded frame. ## 2026-10-15 — Claude: updater survives a module read while the game starts or closes

- Branch `claude/updater-parent-exit-race`, base shared `4f086ae`. Fix to Astra's updater (`Updater/Launcher.cs`) because it turned PR #62 red; for Astra's review.
- CI `native-updater-windows` failed once on `4f086ae` (job 116733698831); three other runs of the same job on that commit passed. `WaitForParent` read `Process.MainModule` and Windows threw `Win32Exception` ERROR_PARTIAL_COPY (299, "Only part of a ReadProcessMemory…"). That error happens while a process is still loading modules or tearing down, so a real update could fail the same way when the game closes as the updater starts.
- `ModulePath` now retries that one error for up to two seconds and returns "exited" if the process ends meanwhile. `WaitForParent` and `AnyGameRunning` both use it. Every other failure is unchanged: a different program still refuses, any other Win32 error still refuses or reports that instances cannot be verified.
- Checks: the launcher compiles as C# 5 with warnings as errors (Roslyn `-langversion:5` against the .NET 4.8 reference assemblies, matching the v4.0.30319 compiler CI uses); Python suite, package and diff-check pass. Not run here: `check_updater_windows.py` (Windows only); CI runs it on the push. Gameplay, networking and saves unchanged.

## 2026-10-15 — Claude: HTTPS room round trip leaves PR CI (Electron game test)

- Branch `claude/ci-drop-https-relay`, base shared `cfd2a76`. Follows the owner's CI direction ("remove those electron game tests if they are just going to cause failures each time").
- Problem: PR #62 `verify` failed on `1f21a6e` in `test:https` (`tests/https-network.ts`): "Snapshot disagreement at tick 0". `src/` and `tests/` were unchanged since the green `d882454`.
- Cause (a race in the test, not the relay): the host broadcasts more than one snapshot at the same tick (on `welcome('host')`, then on the guest's join, both before the clock steps), and the test keeps one expected state per tick (`states.set(tick, ...)`). When the guest receives the earlier tick-0 snapshot it is compared against the later one. Whether that happens depends on timing.
- Why it leaves CI rather than being patched: the test plays the frozen Electron game over the room `/exchange` path. The Unity client uses only `/api/accounts` and `/api/directory` (`NativeAccount.cs`, `NativeAdmin.cs`, `NativeRoomDirectory.cs`).
- Change: `scripts/ci-scope.mjs` no longer selects `relay-full`; PRs that are not docs-only or Unity-only run `verify:relay` (types, the 5 relay test files, the relay build). `verify:relay-full` (adds `test:https`) stays for local use and the manual `workflow_dispatch`. DEVELOPMENT.md updated. If anyone keeps running `test:https`, the fix is to keep every snapshot per tick and accept a match against any of them.
- Checks: `npm run verify:relay` passed (types; 34/34 relay tests; relay build). `ci-scope.mjs` gives `relay` for PR #62's whole diff, `native` for a Unity-only diff and `docs` for an empty one. Local `test:https` runs on the unchanged code passed; the CI failure did not reproduce locally.

## 2026-10-15 — Claude — Expedition chooser camera: swing round to face my pilot while choosing (owner: "Lets swing the camera to us when choosing,")
- Branch `claude/expedition-chooser-camera`, base shared `425cb2d`, fast-forwarded to shared `617fee5` (docs only). Stage 1 of the branch; the owner's later hologram-screen and look-lock direction follows in the next entry.

## 2026-10-14 — Claude — daggers: the sprint's arms held still, the run's rear blade steadied (owner: "Was the dagger run fixed? It still looks like its doing the same thing with the arm"; then "We can probably keep the arms more still (it looks like theyre trying to move the forearms too much with sprinting)")
- Branch `claude/dagger-arm` on shared `c134dc2`, merged with shared `9770b7d` (PR #209 and the DEV tools; no conflicts). Implementation commit `4260b70`. Pushed on the branch; no PR, merge or release. Follows "sprint arms" below (`b72fb1c`, which shipped in the test build).
- **Measured** (scratch probe over the real Core poses: every chain joint on both arms, in chest space and in the heading frame a following camera sees; walk, run, sprint, strafes, backpedal, diagonals, turning, mouse-look sway, lock-on circling, starts and stops, run-sprint-run, jump landings, guard, swings; 60, 144 and 240 Hz and uneven frames; a 20 Hz snapshot replica with its 100 ms buffer, also with late snapshots). Ranked by size:
  1. **The sprint pump (dominant, both arms, every path).** The dagger sprint carry swung each fist 60 cm fore and aft at the 3.7 Hz stride: each elbow flexed 38-41° and each forearm swung 76-82° a stride, 120 cm of fist travel a stride, the blade tips 141-145 cm a stride in the camera's frame. The lift rode `Math.Max(0, cos)`, a kink twice a stride: the forearm's turn rate jumped up to 48,900 °/s² at 240 Hz. The same at every frame rate and on the replica. `b72fb1c` steadied only the blades' lie (the wrist): the pump was left as it was and measures bit-identical before and after it. That is why the owner saw no change.
  2. **The run's rear blade (right hand).** In the daggers' stance the right fist is the rear one: its wrist sits 32-36 cm behind the left in idle and run, and it is the near arm under the shoulder camera. `b72fb1c` treated the left as the back arm. The run carry's lie hung the right blade's tip 25 cm under the floor guard's plane. The blade clearance's floor term (applied with the capture) and `MeleeCapture.KeepBladesOffFloor` (over the leaned, counter-twisted pose) both lifted it, at different points of each stride. The wrist turned through 10.6° a stride (33° of turn), 3.4° of it at twice the stride rate, against the clip's own 4.8° (both corrections off). Strafes and backpedal: 10-16° (23-31° a stride). The tip sat pinned to the floor line while the wrist flicked beneath it.
  3. **The left shoulder shrug.** The run carry damps the hands, not the clavicles, so the left clavicle kept the clip's full shrug: 17-24° a stride. In the run it gave the left elbow 6.8° of flex against the right's 3.1°. Under a held sprint carry it rocks that arm alone, and its forearm's turn rate kinks at the clip's key rate (24,000-26,000 °/s² at 240 Hz).
  4. Shared and **not changed** (other weapons, not the reported symptom): the jump landing hands the arms from the air pose to the ground pose in one frame (56° of forearm and 75 cm of tip in one 60 Hz frame; the sword measures the same: `NativeJumpMotion.Land` starts the landing clip at weight 0). The melee carry's direction blend is not smoothstepped at the bracket ends, so mouse sway across the facing kinks the hands (up to 35,000 °/s² at 240 Hz). The sword, shield and gun sprint lifts keep the `Math.Max(0, cos)` kink. A replica with late snapshots hitches the stride; in the old dagger sprint that showed as 1.6 cm and 2.4° of residual above the stride harmonics.
  - Not a cause: turning while running (the arms ride the chest), the guard while moving (arms fixed), attack recovery blending out (no step above the steady run's), the walk.
- **Fix** (presentation only, daggers only):
  - `NativeSprintMotion` daggers carry: the fists are held low beside the hips and clear of the waist, elbows tucked back. Before, the fists sank up to 14.6 cm into the hip boxes on 76% of frames, and the right blade went 2.8 cm into a thigh. They keep a light 12 cm pump with a smooth lift (`DaggerX`..`DaggerLift`, `DaggerElbowR/L`). The steady blade lies `DaggerRight/DaggerLeft` are kept.
  - `NativeLocomotionCarry`, the daggers' run family: the right blade's lie is tipped back .7 rad about the chest's side axis (`NativeLocoRules.RearBladeTip`, close to the sprint's lie), and both clavicles keep the arms' share of the shrug. The walk family is untouched.
- **Before → after** (probe and new `Tests/SprintArmChecks`; CoreTests `--sprint-arms` prints every measure):
  - Sprint, left/right: elbow flex 37.9/40.9° → 4.4/4.6° a stride, forearm swing 76-82° → 19-20°, fist pump 60 → 12 cm, fist travel 120 → 24 cm a stride, camera-frame tip travel 145/141 → 60/63 cm, forearm turn-rate kink at 240 Hz 48,800/48,000 → 6,200/6,200 °/s². Tips 17-19 cm over the floor guard's plane (6.3 before); blade lies still steady (span ≤.08°, no flick). The same at 60/144/240 Hz, uneven frames and on the replica. Replica with late snapshots: residual 1.6 cm/2.4° → 0.3 cm/0.5°. Per-frame forearm step in a steady sprint 15 → 4°; run-sprint-run blend step 14.6 → 9.4° a frame.
  - Run, rear (right) wrist: ahead 10.6 → 4.8° (33 → 12° a stride), strafe left 14.3 → 3.5, strafe right 10.5 → 4.2, backpedal 15.7 → 4.5, diagonals 7.2/9.3 → 5.2/6.2°. Rear tip travel 51.5 → 21.0 cm a stride (chest). Its tip now rides 9.6 cm over the plane straight ahead; strafe-right and backpedal still touch it but no longer wobble. Left elbow 6.8 → 2.2°. In the camera frame the rear tip now bobs with the body like the front blade (2.4/4.0 cm vs 2.4/2.7 at 1x/2x stride) instead of being pinned to the floor line by a turning wrist.
  - Bit-identical (probe, every scenario and rate): sword, greatsword, shield; the dagger walk, walk strafe and idle.
  - Swing entered from the run: the rear blade's 90 ms windup covers the same total path (189 vs 191 cm) with a higher single-frame peak (107 vs 89 cm). Swing timing unchanged.
- **Paths**: third person at host and guest frame rates and the 20 Hz replica, as above. First person draws neither layer (the generic view arms keep 30% of the captured run, `FirstPersonCarry`, and the sprint is the view sway: daggers bob gain 1, about 1.2 cm sideways and 1.5 cm down). Not changed; not measured in Unity.
- Animation impact: the dagger run and sprint arm and blade poses only. No change to hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement or sprint rules, prediction or networking. The sprint carry still drops for swings, blocks, rolls and stuns.
- Tests: `Tests/SprintArmChecks` now measures, in the sprint, elbow flex ≤8° and forearm swing ≤30° a stride, a fist pump of 8-20 cm and the forearm kink at 240 Hz ≤10,000 °/s². In the run it checks the rear wrist in six directions (≤7°, ≤16° a stride), both elbows ≤4°, both tips ≤40 cm a stride and the left lie's spread. It also checks the blade lies, floor margin, flick and blend, and runs an allocation pass warmed with the identical pass. On the old Core 14 checks fail; all pass on the new one. `SprintMotionChecks` expects the light pump (8-20 cm) instead of the hard one.
- Checks (merged head): `unity-check.sh` runtime+editor OK. `check_relay.py` exit 0, 680 PASS lines (the sprint arm and sprint motion checks and the real WebSocket relay included; managed run 3.6 min). CI layout (the exported index, `docs` removed): `check_relay.py` exit 0, 680 PASS lines. Python 101 OK (1 skipped). `package_source.py` passed (1,942 files; Builds removed). `git diff --check` clean.
- Renders: offline voxel harness over the real Core poses (fxref port, not Unity), scratch `dagger-probe/rend-final/cmp-daggers-{sprint,run,strafe-r}.png`. Each shows before (shipped) and after strips from the side, the front and the shoulder camera. Probe: `dagger-probe/probe`, `arms.py`, `trans.py`, `handrange.py`.
- Not run: Unity Editor, Windows play, two-client play.
- Risks: the held sprint carry and the rear blade's run lie are taste calls (fists beside the hips at (±.34, -.12, .1) in chest space; the run's rear blade trails back like the sprint's). On the voxel boxes, the right knuckle still touches the pelvis belt by up to 3.8 cm on 40% of sprint frames; the blades now clear the legs. Next: the owner's look on Windows. The shared items in 4 are open for a separate task: the jump landing pop, the direction-blend kink, and the sword, shield and gun lift kink.

## 2026-10-14 — Claude — melee cut: the killing swing by its id, the attacker at contact
- Branch `claude/melee-slice-ids` on shared `65f9f13`, which includes Astra's merged PR #205 (`f654074`, "authoritative hit metadata"). Not merged; the lead reviews. Task: bind the melee mesh-slice gib to #205's fields instead of finding the killing blow by time alone. Primary swing Hit/Headshot events carry `Projectile = swing.Id` (an extra strike shares it) and `From` = the attacker's body centre at contact. Presentation only.
- **Ledger (Core `NativeHitLedger`):**
  - It keeps each target's last four melee blows with their swing id (`MeleeBlow.Swing`), and links each Death event to the last damaging Hit in its tick.
  - `Blow()`: when the killing hit carries an id, the blow is that attacker's, with that id, in that tick. A newer blow by another swing no longer wins, and an extra strike's kill takes its own strike. If that swing's blow was never read, there is no blow, rather than another swing's.
  - Id 0 (Q/E kit, E special, plunge, thrown blades, older frames and replays) or no Death read keeps the old rule: the latest blow within 0.02 s.
- **Plan (Core `NativeMeleeSlice`):**
  - `MeleeBlow.From` stays the frame's feet and `Struck` is the hit's `From` (body centre). `Attacker` keeps its rule (an id, and within 2° of the event's direction) and now reports when it used the contact position.
  - The thrown test (beyond reach) reads that same position. Cases without an id plan exactly as before.
- **Docs and comments:** the stale "no hit carries it yet" comments in `MeleeBlow`, the ledger, `Plan`/`Attacker`, `NativeDeathPresentation.MeleeSlice` and `NativeHitPresentation` are updated. In docs/BISECT-GIB.md "Melee cuts", the Astra contract section is replaced by "Exact swing link".
- **Unchanged:** simulation, rules, networking and wire fields. No edits to NativeArena, NativeMelee*, NativeNetworkFrame or NativeFrameCodec. Horde add cuts keep their own last-blow window and do not read the id. Animation impact: none on hit timing, hitboxes, damage, cooldowns, movement or networking.
- **Checks:**
  - Unity runtime and editor compile OK.
  - check_relay exit 0 with 673 PASS lines. Melee bisect has 14,223 checks, up from 14,078 with the new swing-link block: 12 blows across sword, greatsword and daggers, cuts 1–4.
  - Python 101 OK (1 skip); package_source OK (1897 files); `git diff --check` clean.
  - Mutation checks: restoring the time-only `Blow()` fails "the killing hit's swing id finds its blow", and reading the thrown test from the frame fails "the thrown test reads the attacker at contact".
- **Not run:** Unity Editor or PhysX play, Windows, real host/guest multiplayer, and the killcam on a device.
- **Risks:** a busy tick that drops the killing Hit (the 32-per-tick transient event cap) falls back to the time rule, as before. A killing swing whose attacker is missing from the frame now gets the level fallback cut instead of another swing's blow.

## 2026-10-14 — Claude — dressed maps: coincident faces no longer z-fight
- Branch `claude/map-surface-artifacts` on shared `0671054`. Task: the graphical artifacts on the new maps, including the green-panel surface artifacts (2026-10-13). Z-fighting was suspected, not confirmed.
- **Confirmed cause (geometric audit, not the recording):** faces drawn at the same depth. Every block and kit part is a chamfered box through NativeBlockLit.
  - The audit measured what each map draws: blocks as the dressing draws them, kit parts from the Factory, Cyber City and Ward Zero builders, each with its draw's chamfer.
  - It found same-facing faces in one plane, overlapping on their flat parts, in four ways: a part laid flush on its block, two parts of one fitting, blocks running into each other, and exact duplicates.
  - Visible pairs: Brickfall 102 (24.8 m²), Factory about 1,540 (222 m²), Cyber City 116 (8.2 m²), Ward Zero 4,234 (168 m²).
  - Not depth precision or material state: the depths are equal by construction, and the cameras and the shader's depth state are standard.
- **The green panels:**
  - Factory lathes (MapLooks `steel-green`, "machine green"): the hazard collar was a slab whose top lay exactly on each bed top (6.4 m² per lathe, at cover height), so green and stripes fought across all six beds.
  - Also involved: Ward Zero's green tank fluid against the steel caps, Brickfall's green bridge steel against the floors, and Cyber City's planters.
- **Backdrops:** the skylines draw the same way.
  - Before: Brickfall 2,404 pairs (812 m²), Factory 237 (1,046 m², two of its stacked tower stages drawn twice), Cyber City 1,259 (102 m², neon trims flush on the towers).
  - Most are visible from inside the arena.
- **Duplicates:**
  - Ward Zero drew every concourse lane dash five times (each deck emitted the dashes over the whole run: 252 extra boxes) and two posts where rails meet.
  - The Factory drew 6 parts twice.
- **Fix (render only):**
  - **New Core `NativeSurfaceLayers`:** moves only the face meant to be seen, outward by whole 2 mm steps. A kit part goes over its block, a later part over an earlier one, a larger block face over a smaller. Two parts with the same look and drive may go either way. Faces wholly inside another box are skipped.
  - **Where it runs:** blocks are solved alone (`NativeArenaDressing`, Ward Zero menu backdrop); kits are solved over them (the three builders, `layers` default on).
  - **Backdrops:** `NativeSceneryBuilder` now collects its boxes and emits them at the first `Bake`, after the same pass (same emission order). `NativeCyberCityScenery.Build` does the same.
    - Backdrop settings (`NativeSurfaceLayers.Far`): overlaps under 2 cm wide are left alone (sub-pixel at 50 m and beyond), and members meeting at a corner may go either way.
    - Backdrop lifts are capped at 64 mm.
  - **Lift size:** at most 8 mm on maps and 4 mm on backdrops; about 90% of moved faces move 2 mm.
  - **Generators:**
    - The lathe collar is now two strips along the bed sides, so the top stays machine green.
    - Each Ward lane dash sits on its own deck, and rail junctions share one post.
    - The Factory static kit drops exact duplicates.
    - The Factory draw and the layers share `NativeFactoryKit.Bevel`.
- **Preserved:**
  - Block data: colliders, ids (Cyber City `pit-*-stair-*` included), nav, hazards, destructibles and spawns.
  - Cyber City's invisible Cut ramps: collider-only, untouched.
  - Kit parts keep their parent, look, drive and travel.
  - No camera or depth-state change.
- **Checks:**
  - Unity runtime+editor compile OK.
  - check_relay exit 0: 649 PASS, including the new `SurfaceChecks` (36 checks).
  - Python 101 OK (1 skip); package_source OK; `git diff --check` clean; sparse-copy relay 649 PASS.
  - Audit after the fix: 0 coincident visible faces on all four maps, nothing drawn twice, the same every build.
  - Backdrops after: Factory 0 and Cyber City 0. Brickfall keeps 48 same-colour pairs, all facing away from the arena.
  - Cost: in .NET 8 here (Mono not measured), once per map load: Factory kit layers about 25 ms; Brickfall skyline solve about 120 ms (14,629 boxes); Factory skyline 13 ms.
  - Tools: `CoreTests.dll --surface-audit` (before/after report, `differ`, `dupes`), `--scenery` (backdrops) and `--surfaces` (the regression check, 36 checks).
- **Not run:**
  - Unity views from different angles and distances, movement past surfaces, light and shadow inspection, and Windows.
  - The Windows player's depth format was not measured. 2 mm is resolved at any map distance with a float depth buffer, and to about 30 m with a 24-bit one.
  - The owner's Oct 13 recording was not available; it is needed to confirm the artifact seen is this one.

No deployed relay/account service was modified.
